resources.string: Throw three darts a visit at the board. Each part of the board scores: the thin outer ring doubles the number, the thin inner ring trebles it, and the bull in the middle is worth 25 and 50.
Drag on the board to move the reticle, then flick upward to throw. A moderate flick is best. Your hand wobbles a little, shown by the circle around the reticle.
In 501 and 301 count down to exactly zero. You must finish on a double, and going past zero is a bust that sends you back to where the visit began.
In Cricket close 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15 and the bull with three marks each. Once you have closed a number, extra hits score points while a rival still has it open.
Tap Hint for a suggested target and the finishing route. When your three darts are thrown, press Collect darts to pass the turn.
The standard dartboard numbering, with 20 at the top and 3 and 11 beside the bottom, is traditionally credited to a Lancashire carpenter named Thomas Bucknall Ellis in 1896.
Bowl ten frames. In each frame you get up to two balls to knock down all ten pins. Knock them all down with the first ball and it is a strike.
Set the start position, aim, spin and speed with the sliders and press Roll. Or drag across the foot of the lane to place the ball and swipe up: the angle is the aim and a curve adds hook.
For the best chance of a strike, start wide and hook the ball into the pocket between the head pin and the pin beside it.
A spare is clearing the pins with your second ball and scores the next ball as a bonus. A strike scores the next two balls. A perfect game of twelve strikes is 300.
The rack in the corner shows which pins are still standing. Tap Hint for a suggested shot, and turn on Bumpers in the setup to keep the ball out of the gutters.
Ten-pin bowling\'s triangle of pins is a descendant of older nine-pin games; a Connecticut ban on nine-pins in the 1840s is often said to have led to the extra tenth pin.
